page.overview:
Who is Reginna Bel Typolla?

Reginna Bel Typolla or Gina was a Human female from the planet Malthor. After a period off-world in which she became involved in weapons smuggling, she returned to her home planet and became an administrative worker in the spaceport in the city of Fabrillan, where she was recruited by the Rebel Alliance as a member of a sleeper cell designated V-16.

Gina was born on the planet Malthor around 26 BBY. Sometime before 1 BBY she was active as a gunrunner in the Medepiest Uprising, but after surviving that campaign, she returned to Malthor, where she became a uniformed employee of the Fabrillan City Spaceport—specifically, she was the official charged with reviewing the documentation of all vessels docked at the facility, and making administrative copies of their cargo and passenger inventories.

Around 1 BBY, she was recruited by the Alliance to Restore the Republic as a member of Sleeper Cell V-16, tasked with simply sharing the information she had access to. Occasionally, she furnished specific details on Imperial movements through Fabrillan, or on smugglers and cargo pilots who might be useful to the Alliance, but her primary role involved making additional copies of the extensive information she obtained on shipping arriving at the port, which she would dead-drop every few days by discarding an apparently damaged computer memory device.

The clandestine methods Gina used to pass on information meant that she had no direct knowledge of other Alliance agents except her original recruiter, and she was unaware that the material she supplied found its way to Berren Sid Té, who she knew only as the head of a network of street vendors and perhaps a local information broker; she also believed that the Alliance was unware of her past activities as a gunrunner. However, although Sid was not formally told of her identity either, he had been able to work it out relatively easily due to the quantity of information he had access to, and senior Alliance personnel like General Airen Cracken were fully aware of her past—leading to a slight concern that the Empire might have also found out.
